title: Japan’s key services inflation gauge hits 36-year high
html:
The bank’s Governor Kazuo Ueda has signalled the bank’s readiness to keep raising rates to prevent inflation from deviating above its 2% target.

PHOTO: REUTERS

AI generated

TOKYO – A key gauge of Japan’s service-sector inflation jumped 4.2% in October for the fastest annual pace since 1990, data showed on Nov 25, a sign of broadening price pressures that bolster the case for a near-term interest rate hike by the central bank.

The year-on-year rise in the services producer price index, which tracks the prices companies charge each other for services, followed a revised gain of 3.8% in September, data from the Bank of Japan (BOJ) showed.

The increase was driven largely by rising costs of ocean freight transport, leasing and higher hotel charges, the data showed.

The data is closely watched by the bank for clues to what extent companies are passing on rising labour costs to service-related prices.

An index measuring services prices in labour-intensive sectors rose 2.7% in October from a year earlier, accelerating slightly from a 2.6% gain in September, the data showed.

“Firms continue to pass on rising labour costs,” though the pace of price rises in labour-intensive sectors is slower than those for overall services prices, said Kenichiro Ahara, an economist at Dai-ichi Life Research Institute.

“We need to scrutinise whether the pass-through of labour costs continues in a wide range of sectors, and leads to sustained rises in services prices,” he said.

Mounting inflationary pressure for services would add to a steady increase in goods prices.

Annual wholesale inflation rose 7.1% in the year to October, data showed in November, as the Middle East conflict and AI-related demand kept pushing up prices for fuel and semiconductor chips.

The BOJ raised its policy rate to 1.25% in September after a June hike, for a shorter interval than the roughly twice-a-year hikes of 2024 and 2025.

The bank’s Governor Kazuo Ueda has signalled its readiness to keep raising rates to prevent inflation from deviating above its 2% target.

A majority of analysts polled by Reuters expect the BOJ to raise rates in December and follow up with another hike by end-March. Many see the terminal rate at around 1.75% or 2%. REUTERS
summary: The increase was driven largely by rising costs of ocean freight transport, leasing and higher hotel charges.
